title: Taking Counsel
body:
Taking Counsel

With the thirteen-year term completed, the Pandavas shed their disguises and settled openly in Upaplavya, a prosperous city within the Matsya territory. From there, they sent emissaries to summon their friends and relatives. Sree Krishna and Balarama arrived from Dwaraka, accompanied by Subhadra and the young hero Abhimanyu. King Drupada of Panchala arrived with his divisions, bringing Sikhandin and Draupadi's sons. Before the assembled heroes, the wedding of Abhimanyu and Princess Uttara was celebrated with Vedic rites, solidifying a powerful alliance between the Matsya, Panchala, and Yadava dynasties.
The wedding celebrations concluded, the kings met in conclave in Virata's assembly hall to deliberate on their next course of action. Sree Krishna rose to address the hushed gathering, presenting a balanced and righteous argument. He reminded them that Yudhishthira had been cheated at the game board and deprived of his legitimate share of the kingdom. Yet, Krishna emphasised that Yudhishthira had no desire for violence, and proposed that they should send an able and upright emissary to Hastinapura to persuade Duryodhana to a peaceful settlement by restoring half the kingdom to the Pandavas.
Balarama supported Krishna's plea, urging a tactful approach and pointing out that Yudhishthira had played the dice game obstinately, despite the warnings of his well-wishers, and therefore should supplicate for his rights. This remark provoked a fierce and indignant response from Satyaki, who declared that Yudhishthira was not a mendicant and need not beg. Satyaki argued that allowing the Kauravas to keep the stolen kingdom was as unjust as confirming a thief in the possession of his booty, and urged immediate preparations for war.
King Drupada supported Satyaki's resolute stance, noting that soft words would never bring Duryodhana to reason. He advised that while they should send a learned Brahmin envoy from his court to Hastinapura to fulfil the formal demands of diplomacy, they must simultaneously prepare for war with unremitting vigour. Sree Krishna concurred, noting that they had equal ties of affection with both sides, and returned to Dwaraka, leaving Drupada's envoy to convey the formal peace terms.
